content: The test image shows a stem at the soil line with white cottony mycelium and small dark spherical structures (sclerotia). This strongly suggests Southern Blight. Let me confirm with one reference image.

The test image clearly shows:
- White cottony mycelium on the stem at the soil line
- Small, round, dark spherical sclerotia (mustard-seed sized) embedded in the mycelium
- Stem decay at/near soil level

This is a textbook match for Southern Blight caused by *Sclerotium rolfsii*. The key diagnostic features — white cottony mycelial mat with small spherical sclerotia turning black — perfectly match the Southern_Blight description. Sclerotinia_Timber_Rot produces larger, rice-grain-shaped sclerotia inside the stem, not the small round ones visible here.
